project.name: webspace-engine
project.description: A 3D world creation framework that turns standard HTML into immersive 3D environments. The HTML document is both the source of truth and the persistence layer; CSS transforms on tags like , ,

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Project README. Pitches the engine as 'edit an HTML file as a 3D world.' Highlights: HTML document is the source of truth and persistence layer; CSS transforms on <model> tags carry pose; toroidal wrapped world; vox editing with peer presence; emoji rendered as extruded voxmoji meshes; greedy meshing collapses voxel chunks. Describes the FastNoise + chunked terrain generator.

nodes.name: todo.txt
nodes.summary: Author's working notes. Hints at design choices in the smoothvoxels mesher, the WebRTC delta sync, the voxmoji alpha hash. Mentions 'smooth voxel mesher is randomized' as a known issue and references the toroidal world wrap.

nodes.name: mesher.js
nodes.summary: Greedy mesher for voxel terrain. The function GreedyMesh sweeps three axes, builds a 2D boundary mask per slice, and emits axis-aligned quads by lexicographic run-length expansion. Crucially the mask stores integers from a caller-provided getSplitKey function — not booleans — so the inner equality test (cv === vals[n + w]) does whatever discrimination the caller packed into those integers. Max quad size capped at 12 to prevent seams when curving.
nodes.languageNotes: The trick: mesher does not know about color. Caller decides what to pack.

nodes.name: GreedyMesh
nodes.summary: Three-axis sweep of a voxel chunk. For each axis, builds two parallel Int32Arrays: mask[n] = whether there is a face here (boundary cell), vals[n] = the discriminating integer the caller chose to attach to that face. Then walks the mask lexicographically and grows rectangles: width extends while mask[n+w] is set and vals match; height extends row-by-row checking the same. Emits one quad per maximal rectangle, zeros the mask under it. The whole color-aware merging story lives in two equality tests on vals.
nodes.languageNotes: The clever bit is that the loop never inspects color; it compares integers from getSplitKey.

nodes.name: getSplitKey
nodes.summary: Constructs a 32-bit integer per voxel that packs type in the low byte and r, g, b in successive bytes: chunk.voxels[voxel] | (r << 8) | (g << 16) | (b << 24). Returns 0 for air (which the mesher reads as 'no face here'). This is the function passed as the split-key callback to GreedyMesh. The mesher's equality test on these integers does color-aware face merging without any color-comparison code.
nodes.languageNotes: Cleverness: a single shift-and-OR sequence stores all face-identity bits in one int.

nodes.name: chunk.js
nodes.summary: Storage layout for one 64x64x64 voxel chunk. Backing storage is one Uint8Array of length 64^3 * 8 = ~2 MiB. Eight bytes per voxel: type, r, g, b, lr (low-LOD r), lg, lb, palette. The Mesher() constructor in this file wires up getType/getColor/getSplitKey/getPalette callbacks the mesher then calls per-cell.

nodes.name: generator.js
nodes.summary: Procedural terrain generator. Uses FastNoise + a tiledSimplex projection that lifts 2D (x,z) coordinates onto a 4D simplex via (cos, sin) pairs — the trick that lets the toroidal world wrap seamlessly. Computes plateau / bridge / terrain heights, picks colors from a per-cell noise of the palette. The 4D simplex is the entire reason the noise is continuous across the wrap.
nodes.languageNotes: Wrapping 2D noise requires lifting to a torus; cos/sin parameterizes that as 4D.

nodes.name: tiledSimplex
nodes.summary: tiledSimplex(x, z, x1, x2, z1, z2) returns the magnitude of a 4D simplex noise sample where the 4 coordinates are derived by remapping x and z through COS_TABLE and SIN_TABLE. Effectively projects 2D coordinates onto a torus before sampling, which is the mathematical reason the terrain has no visible seam at the wrap boundary.

nodes.name: dom-serialize-system.js
nodes.summary: Every 250 ms (FLUSH_DELAY), this system polls every registered entity's object3D matrix. When matrix is dirty (set by user drag), it decomposes pos/rot/scale and writes a CSS transform: translate3d(...) string into the matching DOM element's style attribute via setAttributeIfChanged. There is no model layer; the DOM is the model.
nodes.languageNotes: Producer of DOM mutations that the persistence MutationObserver later consumes.

nodes.name: atom-access-manager.js
nodes.summary: Hosts the engine's persistence-side MutationObserver. Observes document.documentElement with subtree+childList+attributes+characterData all true. Filters out styled-components <style> removals; any other mutation sets documentIsDirty = true, dispatches a 'document-dirty-state-changed' CustomEvent, and schedules a setTimeout(write, MAX_WRITE_RATE_MS=10000) — the entire save subsystem. write() base64-encodes documentElement.outerHTML and POSTs to GitHub.
nodes.languageNotes: Cleverness: there is no serialize function. The DOM is the file. The observer + 10s debounce is the whole save subsystem.

nodes.name: AtomAccessManager.mutationObserver
nodes.summary: The MutationObserver callback that does the entire persistence triage. Walks each MutationRecord, ignores styled-components <style> removals, and on any other mutation sets dirty=true and schedules write 10s out. write() serializes documentElement.outerHTML and uploads it to GitHub via 4 REST API calls (blob, tree, commit, ref). No diff, no patch format.

nodes.name: world-importer.js
nodes.summary: The 'load' side of the persistence story. There is no deserialize function: the browser parses the HTML, and this WorldImporter walks document.body's children, reads transform out of each tag's style, and spawns the corresponding A-Frame entity at the parsed position. The fact that there's no symmetric load function is the design.

nodes.name: vox-system.js
nodes.summary: Voxel object subsystem. Hosts a 32-slot ring buffer (DELTA_RING_BUFFER_LENGTH=32) for delta sync. Conflict resolution: peers exchange voxel-painting deltas over WebRTC; each entry in the ring buffer holds a finalized delta at a particular revision. When a remote delta arrives, the system walks the ring oldest-first and commutatively merges via Voxels.mergeWith for any same-revision entries; the tiebreak is deterministic by revision ordering. There is no separate journal — the ring is the merge history.
nodes.languageNotes: Cleverness: a fixed-size ring carries the entire merge history; old conflicts age off the end and that is correct because no one will merge against revisions 32-deep.

nodes.name: performVoxelsConflictResolution
nodes.summary: The convergent conflict resolution for voxel painting. Walks the 32-slot ring buffer oldest-first; for slots at the same revision as the incoming delta, calls voxels.mergeWith(...) with a stable targetAlwaysWins = ringRevision > revision tiebreak. The finalized merged voxels are then written into the ring at deltaRingIndex and the cursor advances.

nodes.name: edit-ring-manager.js
nodes.summary: Presence / handshake for collaborative editing. Manages joining the sync ring, requesting initial doc snapshots from existing members, deciding genesis (when no one else is present). For cold-start races where two clients independently become genesis: the tiebreak is clientId > NAF.clientId — whichever client has the numerically larger client ID becomes authoritative; the other requests a full doc and discards its own work.
nodes.languageNotes: A single inequality is the entire cold-start tiebreak.

nodes.name: voxmoji-system.js
nodes.summary: Renders emoji as 3D extruded meshes. When the user types an emoji into the DOM, the system rasterizes its SVG, computes an alpha-mask hash from the binary pixel coverage, and uses that hash to pool meshes: emoji with identical alpha silhouettes share a single 3D mesh and instanced draw call, even when their colors differ. RGB differences are stored in a per-instance 4x4 texture atlas. Result: 200 colored smiley emoji become one draw call.
nodes.languageNotes: Cleverness: mesh sharing keyed by silhouette, not by visual appearance.

nodes.name: wrapped-entity-system.js
nodes.summary: Toroidal world wrap. The world is a finite 8-chunk x 64-voxel grid (512 m square) but the player walks infinitely. Each frame, wrappable scene objects get repositioned to whichever of nine candidate world-space copies (a 3x3 lattice) is closest to the player. Combined with the 4D simplex noise in generator.js the world feels continuous.

nodes.name: github-writeback.js
nodes.summary: The 'save to disk' implementation. Takes a full HTML string and writes it to a GitHub repository via four API calls: POST git/blobs, POST git/trees, POST git/commits, PATCH git/refs. No diff is computed. The whole file becomes a new whole file. Used only when atom-access-manager's debounce fires.

nodes.name: terra.worker.js
nodes.summary: Web Worker that runs the terrain generator and mesher off the main thread. Maintains a jobPriorities Map; each tick scans for the min-priority pending job and runs that one, yielding to the next tick otherwise. Effectively a cooperative coroutine scheduler. Caches finished chunks in IndexedDB so subsequent loads skip noise sampling.

nodes.name: dom-utils.js
nodes.summary: Misc DOM helpers including pushHubMetaUpdateIntoDOM. When a peer broadcasts an update_hub_meta message, this writes the change into <head>'s <meta> tags — and a SECOND MutationObserver in atom-metadata.js fires on those changes and dispatches hub_meta_refresh, which fans out to atmosphere/sky/spawn-point subscribers. Local and remote hub-metadata changes converge at the same line of code.

nodes.name: atom-metadata.js
nodes.summary: The second MutationObserver in the codebase. Watches document.head for <meta name='webspace.*'> changes and dispatches a hub_meta_refresh CustomEvent that drives the atmosphere, sky color, spawn point. Used by both local UI changes and remote peer updates.
